key_insight: Label-free persona and knowledge directions can detect complementary signals of LLM deception, but their reliability varies by model and wording.
engineering_relevance: Activation-based directions offer a low-cost complement to supervised lie detectors, but require model-specific validation and tests that separate deception from response phrasing.
method: Expand an honest/deceptive persona bank with roles that conceal known information, then derive middle-layer persona directions.
Derive a knowledge direction by contrasting answerable and unanswerable questions followed by identical scripted denials.
Evaluate individual and summed directions against supervised probes and random-direction controls.
evidence_signal: Across four models on Liars’ Bench, persona directions outperformed single-dataset probes on three; summed persona and knowledge directions outperformed same-depth supervised probes on all four, although one comparison was near chance.
watch_item: Persona signals largely tracked wording on knowledge-denial tasks; the expanded bank’s gain on Llama was within random-widening variability, and the summed direction lagged the probe on held-out lies.
paper_title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
